POST /api/support/call-sessions/resume lets a support_agent rotate the token of any attacker-selected session id (prisma.session.update at line 1530) and receive a fresh valid cookie for that user, hijacking arbitrary accounts (including admins) with no binding of the session to the agent's authorized scope.

PATCH /api/products/:id/inventory-adjustment (requireRole vendor_manager/admin) looks up any product by attacker-controlled id and mutates inventory with no vendor-scoping predicate; safe sibling applyProductInventoryAdjustmentScoped (line 1772) adds canReadVendorScoped, confirming the defect.

PATCH /api/store/:handle/tagline-quick-edit (requireAuth only) authorizes editing any vendor's tagline via client-supplied body.accountType==='vendor_owner'; any authenticated user, including buyers, can set that field and edit another vendor's storefront. Safe sibling applyStorefrontTaglineEditVerified (line 1798) uses canReadVendorScoped.

An HTTP response discloses data the caller is not entitled to receive: Response body includes continuityId, a session/continuity credential stored as a tokenHash in the session table, and the body is not narrowed to a non-sensitive projection.

POST /api/orders/activity-search builds the Prisma where clause as { buyerId: req.user!.id, ...req.body }, so an attacker-supplied buyerId in the request body overrides the authenticated scope and returns another user's orders; safe sibling searchOrderActivityFeedScoped (line 2097) validates via zod, confirming the defect.
